outcome: Time from rocuronium administration to TOF (Train-of-Four) points (T3 disappearance, T1/T2 reappearance)
Maternal rocuronium concentration (before cord clamping, at discharge)
cohort: The study included 18 patients undergoing general anesthesia for cesarean section, with their fetuses also considered in the outcomes.
finding: High-dose (1.0 mg/kg) rocuronium, while resulting in faster onset and prolonged duration of blockade, higher rocuronium concentrations in both maternal and umbilical veins, and lower remifentanil use, did not show negative effects on fetal (Apgar scores, blood gas) or maternal (PACU stay) outcomes compared to the conventional dose during cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study specifically investigated the effects of different rocuronium doses during cesarean section, concluding that a high dose (1.0 mg/kg) had no negative effects on the fetus and mother undergoing this mode of birth.
